purpose: Read-only local OpenCode CLI conformance; provider is a synthetic API-key fixture backed only by a loopback HTTP server.

release.checksum_note: Asset SHA-256 is for the compressed tarball; extracted ELF SHA-256 is a different object.

profiles.source_auth_fixture: two synthetic records; selected fixture record is type api with a non-empty fake key
profiles.copied_auth: one selected provider record, exactly fields type and key; fake key value not recorded
profiles.config_dir_contents: canonical OpenCode .gitignore only; both directories mounted read-only
profiles.home: read-only, with only XDG data/state/cache writable overlays
profiles.system_config: synthetic private /etc/opencode contained a canary, foreign MCP and allow-all permissions; production helper empty mask overlaid it

real_cli_run.runner: OpenCode 1.19.4 under bubblewrap with a profile generated by the current Rust helper; production Python helper isolation and debug-config conformance were verified separately.
command_summaries: opencode --pure run --format json --title OrgBots --model fixture/fake-model -- <synthetic fresh prompt>
opencode --pure run --format json --model fixture/fake-model --session <CLI session id> -- <synthetic resume prompt>

mcp_pure_smoke: real OpenCode --pure mcp list connected to a synthetic local stdio JSON-RPC server; zero provider calls

reproducibility.bwrap_profile: read-only root; production helper HOME/config masks; synthetic /etc bind injected only inside test namespace
reproducibility.mcp_tool_command: opencode --pure run --format json --title OrgBots --model fixture/fake-model -- <synthetic prompt>; test profile adds orgbot_room with local fixture stdio command and orgbot_room_* allow; title override is fresh-run only

title_request_regression.effect: The fresh session no longer makes the extra model request that was absent from parsed step_finish usage.
